title: Purposeful observation: positive-list subscriptions, factual evidence only
summary: Browser monitoring is an authorised positive-list subscription, not generic journey surveillance. Only offered observation points and fields may be emitted; accepted records remain factual evidence for downstream Interaction Event/effect assessment.
invariants: No production capture-everything mode: an unregistered/unsubscribed point produces no observation traffic.
Observation definitions state authorised purpose, allowed fields and evidence strength.
Disabled points should return before expensive payload construction.
Accepted observations are factual events; Wire UI does not infer frustration, dark patterns, brand effect or commercial conclusions.
Browser evidence is client-observed/application-asserted and must not be confused with server business fact.
Collection authority does not imply interpretation or intervention authority.
examples: SUPPORT_CONTENT_VIEWED, SYSTEM_ERROR_PRESENTED, ORDER_FAILURE and SERVICE_CANCEL_STARTED are suitable positive-list facts when justified.
Mouse movement, arbitrary scroll depth or generic cart hesitation are not automatically justified merely because they are observable.

provenance.claim: Executable positive-list observation plan, field allow-list validation and downstream-assessment boundary.
Subscription architecture includes observation plans and the JS module provides positive-list capture.
Interaction Event keeps access-point instrumentation external and preserves assessments as assessments rather than facts.
